title: MRM + SKY130 driver, 53 GBd NRZ
description: Microring modulator driven by a real SKY130 CMOS inverter at 53.125 GBd — the transmitter that examples/mrm_tdec_sky130.py optimizes for OMA - TDEC

notes.title: 53.125 GBd NRZ microring transmitter — what this testbench does
lines: PRBS1 drives a real SKY130 inverter (MP/MN, BSIM4.8 via OSDI).
Its output node vdrv is the ring electrode, so RING1's resonance
swings by dl_dv_pm = 45 pm/V across the 1.8 V rail. LAS1 is parked
-33 pm off the cold resonance, on the slope, so that swing becomes
optical amplitude at the through port (probe popt). PD1 + RL1 turn
it back into a voltage (probe vout).
Open the Eye tab: the UI is 1/baud = 18.8 ps, set from the top-bar
baud field. The eye is visibly ISI-limited, and that is the real
result — the measured electrode edge is ~16 ps 20-80% against an
18.8 ps UI, so at this rate the 130 nm / 1.8 V driver is the
bottleneck, not the ring (whose photon-lifetime f_3dB is 44.5 GHz).
TDEC objectives ARE available in the Optimize pane: switch Analysis ->
Optimize and set  objective = omatdec:popt  (OMA - TDEC in dBm,
maximized -- the spec-line number) or  tdec:popt  (TDEC in dB,
minimized -- a diagnostic). Any optical probe works; an electrical one
is rejected, since TDEC is measured on optical power.
BUT read this before trusting a canvas optimum. Measured on this
design: over a 202 UI transient the objective is NOT reliable. A
kappa2 sweep at fixed lock point gives
and 0.12 sitting 0.4 dB below both neighbours is not physics -- a
coupling sweep is smooth. It survives lowering the assumed receiver
noise S (which moves the saturation floor from -8.52 to -15.5 dBm and
leaves the same 4 dB outlier), so it is the short record, not the
floor: stateye's level estimation needs far more symbols than a
browser-length transient affords once the eye is this closed.
So the canvas is for building intuition, and
examples/mrm_tdec_sky130.py -- full-period PRBS-13, 8191 bits -- is
the authoritative optimizer. The objective itself is the same code
(photonflux.tdec); only the record length differs. On a more open eye
(drop --baud, or widen the driver) the canvas optimize is usable.
Also worth turning by hand:
RING1.kappa2  0.076 is critical coupling for this ring; below it
undercoupled (high ER, low OMA), above the reverse.
MP1.w_um / MN1.w_um  driver strength -- deliberately NOT in the
optimize box: a new (W,L) pair compiles a fresh
SKY130 card (41-80 s once, then cached), too slow
for an inner loop. The script does those as a
discrete outer grid.
